name: Object pronouns
intro: Subject → object: I → me, you → you, he → him, she → her, it → it, we → us, they → them. After a verb (I like her) and after a preposition (with them).

questions.prompt: Tom is nice. I like ___. (he)
Where is Amira? I can't see ___. (she)
My parents live in Leeds. I visit ___ every week. (they)
Can you help ___, please? (I)
Liam and I are at home. Call ___ later! (we)
This pizza is great. Do you want ___? (it)
This present is for ___, Mei. (you)

name: Verbs with two objects
intro: give, send, show, tell, buy, bring: person first (give me the book), or the thing first with to or for (give the book to me, buy a present for her). With it or them: give it to me.

questions.prompt: Can you pass ___ the salt, please? (I)
It's Kwame's birthday. Let's buy ___ a cake. (he)
Priya wants to see the photos. Show them to ___. (she)
I lent my bike ___ Tom last week. (lend something to someone)
Mei made a cup of tea ___ her mum. (make something for someone)
That's my phone! Give ___ back to me, please. (the phone)

name: Verbs + prepositions
intro: Some verbs always take the same preposition: wait for, listen to, depend on, look after, agree with, laugh at. Learn the verb and its preposition together.

questions.prompt: Hurry up! The taxi is waiting ___ us outside. (wait for)
Priya listens ___ the radio in the car. (listen to)
We might have a picnic. It depends ___ the weather. (depend on)
Can you look ___ my cat while I'm away? (look after)
I'm sorry, but I don't agree ___ you. (agree with)
Please don't laugh ___ me. I'm doing my best! (laugh at)

name: The passive: all tenses and modals
intro: The passive is a form of be + past participle. Only be changes for the tense: is being done, has been done, will be done. With a modal verb: must be done, can be done.

questions.prompt: The kitchen ___ painted at the moment, so we're eating in the garden. (now, in progress)
Good news! Your parcel ___ sent. It left the warehouse this morning. (present perfect)
The exam results ___ published next Friday. (future)
This form ___ signed by a parent, or it isn't valid. (necessary)
When I arrived at the garage, my car ___ repaired, so I had to wait. (past, in progress)

name: Third conditional and wish
intro: Third conditional, for an unreal past: If + past perfect, would have + past participle (If I had known, I would have come). wish + past simple is about now, wish + past perfect is about the past, and wish + would is about other people's annoying habits.

questions.prompt: If I ___ about the party, I would have come. (know)
If you had asked me, I ___ helped you.
I wish I ___ a bit taller. (be, now)
If only I ___ more free time at the moment! (have)
I wish my neighbours ___ stop playing loud music at night.

name: Relative clauses
intro: who for people, which for things. that works for both (the man that…, the bus that…). When the pronoun is the object, you can leave it out: the film (that) we saw.

questions.prompt: Kwame is the friend ___ lives next door to me. (a person)
This is the train ___ goes to Brighton. (a thing)
Do you know the woman ___ works in the bakery? (a person)
I've lost the keys ___ you gave me. (things)
The phone ___ I bought last week has already broken. (a thing)

name: Phrasal verbs
intro: A verb + a small word (up, down, on, off, for) makes a new meaning: get up, sit down, turn on, take off, look for. With it or them, the small word goes after: turn it on.

questions.prompt: My alarm rings at 6.30, but I get ___ at 7. (get up)
It's dark in here. Can you turn ___ the light? (turn on)
Please take ___ your shoes. The floor is clean. (take off)
I can't find my keys. I'm looking ___ them everywhere. (look for)
Come in and sit ___, please. (sit down)
